beats.vo: A wider path is a reason to space orders further apart, not to load each line harder. Last page, two bands shared one inventory line. This lesson changes the step when the path gets wider, and it keeps inventory per level from rising. On the diagram for this beat, look for a calm weave beside a wider weave, the wider one with fewer rungs. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Sketch both weaves and mark which one has the wider step. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. This is not a claim that a wider step makes the next day safer. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Hook. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

The house span is nine and a half percent, from nineteen gaps at a half of one percent. Twenty order lines make nineteen gaps. You multiply the step by the gaps, not by the lines. On the diagram for this beat, look for twenty lines with nineteen marked gaps, the span labelled nine and a half percent, stamped Example. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write 19 gaps, 0.5 percent step, 9.5 percent span, and the word Example. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. Counting lines as gaps makes the band one step too tall. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to House span. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

If you cut the step to a quarter of one percent and keep that same span, the gap count is thirty-eight and the order count is thirty-nine. That arithmetic is the check. Forty orders would be a wider span, not the same span. On the diagram for this beat, look for the same band with finer gaps, the count 38 written on the gaps and 39 on the lines, stamped Example. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Write 38 gaps and 39 lines, then write: this is a counting example. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. These figures are not levels to trade. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Half the step. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.

When the example path gets wider, one approach is to widen the step and to cut the count so inventory per level does not rise. The wide case holds the same or smaller inventory on each rung. It does not load the line harder. On the diagram for this beat, look for two columns, calm and wide, the wide column with a longer gap and a smaller stack on each rung. The shapes are the lesson. If a shape is only decoration, it does not belong on this frame. Leave size per level the same or smaller in the wide case, and write that sentence. Mark the page Example, so a later reader cannot mistake the sketch for a recommendation to trade an asset or these levels. A wider path is not an invitation to put more on every line. Say the opening line once more, and point at the part that belongs to Widen and cut. If you cannot point yet, do not move on. The point of the beat is the pointing.
